title: Travelers Are Taking Trips Just to Buy Souvenirs
paragraphs: Bringing home a souvenir has long been part of the travel experience. However, for some travelers, the souvenir is no longer just a reminder of a trip; it has become the main reason for taking the trip in the first place.

In October 2026, the travel search company Skyscanner released its Travel Trends 2027 report, which is based on its search data and research involving more than 28,000 travelers worldwide. One of the trends it identified is what it calls "pilgra-merch," a combination of the words "pilgrimage" and "merchandise." It refers to journeys taken specifically to buy products and souvenirs that are only available in a particular place.

According to media reports on the research, the trend appears to be particularly strong in some countries. In India, for example, 80% of travelers surveyed said they had visited a particular destination or store to buy an exclusive item, including 84% of Gen Z respondents. Nearly half of the Indian respondents also said they would consider flying three to six hours to buy something that was not available anywhere else. In Canada, meanwhile, 35% of travelers reportedly said they had taken a trip specifically to buy items they could not get at home.
Examples of such items mentioned by Skyscanner include tote bags from the American supermarket chain Trader Joe's and merchandise from the famous Ritz hotel in Paris.

The trend is also linked to social media, where people like to show off unique items that others cannot easily get. At the same time, mass-produced souvenirs, such as fridge magnets, appear to be losing their appeal.

However, travelers looking for authentic local products should be careful. In 2022, for example, an Australian government report found that up to 75% of souvenirs sold as Indigenous products were fakes.
Moreover, it should be noted that the full details of the survey, including the exact questions asked, have not been widely published, so the figures should be treated with some caution.
